items: Eratosthenes' calculation of Earth's circumference around 240 BCE using shadow angles at Syene and Alexandria is a frequently tested advanced concept.
Questions often test the lunar eclipse phenomenon: only a sphere casts a circular shadow in every orientation.
Remember that ships disappearing bottom-first (hull before mast) over the horizon directly demonstrates physical surface curvature.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Earth casts a circular shadow on the Moon during a lunar eclipse, which only a spherical body can consistently produce.
Ships disappearing bottom-first over the horizon provides clear physical evidence of Earth's surface curvature.
Circumnavigation confirms the spherical shape by enabling continuous travel in one direction back to the starting point.
Latitude-dependent star visibility and global time zone differences further prove the curved surface.
Around 240 BCE, Eratosthenes remarkably estimated Earth's circumference using shadow angles at Syene and Alexandria.

blocks.content: Around 240 BCE, Eratosthenes calculated Earth's circumference using shadow angles at Syene and Alexandria. His estimate was remarkably close to modern measurements — a favorite higher-level exam fact.
